description.narrative: Reporting is an important management tool which is used to inform relevant government officials and other stakeholders about the results being achieved by individual projects and the programme as a whole. For project partners, it is compulsory to use the prescribed Orange Knowledge annual report format in order to report on project achievements. The annual report also provides valuable data on the financial situation of the project. Based on an analysis of the project performance in relation to the project output(s) and expected outcome(s), a revision of the project work plan may be suggested by the project partners. The consequences of a possible revision on the project work plan and budget must be made clear in the annual report. Nuffic monitors outputs and outcomes and not activities . Therefore, the main focus of the annual report must be on the achievement of the project’s output(s) and planned outcome(s). The information provided in the annual reports of the projects is used by Nuffic to monitor the progress of the project and to inform the Ministry of Foreign Affairs and other stakeholders about the output(s) and outcome(s) being achieved by individual projects and the Orange Knowledge programme as a whole. Please note that if project progress is in accordance with the original planning, reporting requirements are minimal. Only in case of deviations from the planning, more elaboration is demanded. In the grant award letter, the dates for submission of the annual reports are mentioned. In case of a three-year project, between 5-7 reports are obligatory. The first report (0) is a very short report which focuses on specific conditions and/or recommendations in the grant. There is no need to report on progress in achieving outputs and outcomes, which is done in the first annual report. As annex to the report 0, the consortium agreements between the partners should be submitted. The final report must reflect on the entire project period.

In this section (maximum 1000 words), please provide a global overview of the project progress **per output**. To what extent have they been achieved? Comment on the activities that have taken place and the most important milestones.

In this paragraph we provide a global overview of the project progress per output:
1. Output 1: Training Propartif and Training of Trainers: 100% achieved - Exceeded our expectations. Activities below a, b and c (PMN training) were added additionally to the proposed activities. 1. Additional activity for training interactively online (Nov 2020) - 20 participants (12 male / 8 female) -> Also, internal Ombudsman RI training took place online in most cases and therefore there was a need for enhancing the online training capabilities of the master trainers. 2. Additional ToT for BIT (investigators) training (Jan 2021) - 18 participants (12 male / 6 female) -> To enhance the capacity of Ombudsman RI Basic Investigation trainers to train new Ombudsman Assistants online. 3. Basic training in Propartif and Training of Trainers
- Microteaching - (18-20 Jan 2021 and 10-11 Feb 2022) (12 male / 10 female) and (11 male / 10 female) -> for ORI trainers to practice facilitating online training and give each other feedback in preparation for the internal (online) Propartif training for Ombudsman staff
- Propartif training Jakarta Offline (May 2021) - 40 participants (22 male / 18 female)
- Online training on Propartif (Feb 2022) - 90 participants (52 male / 38 female)
- PMN certification training in Mediation and Conflict Resolution (Mar 2022) - 10 participants (6 male / 4 female)
1. Advanced training (Mediating in cases of power differences and intercultural mediation)
- Intercultural mediation and dealing with power differences - (May 2022)- 13 participants (7 male / 6 female)
1. Output 2: Revision and adjustment of the current Propartif materials: 100% achieved
- In preparation for the refresher training “Training Interactively Online”, a draft training programme was developed to deliver Propartif training online. This draft has been reviewed, revised and finalised. The final version has been used to deliver online Propartif training for 130 participants.
1. Output 3: Seminar on Improving public service delivery for marginalised and discriminated groups 75 % achieved 1. Webinar Internasional: Maintaining Discrimination as a form of maladministration and the role of Ombudsman supervision. This webinar was intended to reveal how the Ombudsman works in monitoring discrimination, which is a form of maladministration. As it is known that the Ombudsman is the fourth branch of power which not only supervises the implementation of public services carried out by the other three branches of power in the Trias Politica concept, but also through its role (both philosophically and operationally) has the opportunity to take a role in high-level politics, and at the policy level. In this supervisory role, ORI collaborates with three other branches of power in the check and balance process. As stated by Remac and Lamgbroek, the Ombudsman is "a kind of auxiliary component to the checks and balances between the distinct but cooperating state powers". Second, the Ombudsman is also called "a guardian of quality performance in public administration." Instead of the National Ombudsman of the Netherlands, Prof. Adriaan Bedner from Van Vollenhoven Institute Leiden University provided a keynote speech. 2. 1 Revised Ombudsman RI policy aiming at improving access to public services for marginalised and/or discriminated groups
- N/A. We weren’t able to revise a policy as part of the project.
1. Output 4: 49 First-line complaint handlers have advanced skills and knowledge on: 100% achieved.
- Facilitating training for First-line complaint handlers (June 2022)
- National Land Agency or BPN 28 participants (June 2022)- (14 male / 4 female)
- Administrator of SP4N-Lapor! of National Public Service Complaint Management System (June 2022), consists of 5 Agencies: ORI, Ministry of State Apparatus Empowerment and Bureaucratic Reform, Presidential Staff Office, Ministry of Communication and Information Technology, and Ministry of Internal Affairs - 21 participants (14 male / 7 female)
- Output 5: Outreach events: 100% achieved
- Outreach event in South Kalimantan; Dissemination of understanding of the “New” “Propartif” Approach (Progressive and Participatory). It was held in Banjarmasin, South Kalimantan, on November 25th, 2021, at Galaxy Hotel.
The event was attended by ORI's commissioner, Dadan Suparjo Suharmawijaya, along with Head of Partnership, Gunawan Siallagan, and Fahmi Shahab from PMN as speaker. The event was held hybrid, with around 40 people attending offline at Galaxy Hotel.
- 2) Coordination of accelerating the settlement of public service complaints through SP4N-LAPOR! through a Propartive and Simple Approach to the Indonesian Ombudsman
- Outreach event in Central Java; The outreach activity for the Progressive and Participatory Approach was carried out on December 14, 2021, in the city of Semarang, with the theme “Progressive and Participative Approach (Propartif) of the Indonesian Ombudsman in creating a pleasant relationship between the community and service providers. The speakers were Dadan Suparjo Suharmawijaya (member of the Ombudsman) and Sabarudin Hulu (Senior Assistant to the Ombudsman of Central Java). The socialization activity was attended by representatives from 35 (thirty-five) Regencies/Cities and 1 (one) Provincial Government, as well as Ministries/Institutions namely the Central Java Regional Police, the National Land Agency Regional Office, the Central Java Ministry of Law and Human Rights Regional Office, all The number of participants is approximately 60 (sixty) participants.
